body:
The direction should be right, since we agreed on it during the animation meeting.

I suggest creating a base class called `AnimationNodeObserver` and extending it. After that, it would be useful to adopt this approach in `Transition` and `BlendSpace` as well, so that signals can be triggered when the highest-priority port changes; See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111893#issuecomment-3939530482.

At last, it would be better to include the following in the description of the NodeOneShot documentation: `If you want to use signals, you can use [AnimationNodeObserverOneShot].` The same applies to each AnimationNode.

> I suggest creating a base class called `AnimationNodeObserver` and extending it. After that, it would be useful to adopt this approach in `Transition` and `BlendSpace` as well, so that signals can be triggered when the highest-priority port changes 

Would anything live in that base class or would it stay empty for now? I omitted the shared base class in my first pass since the signal signatures would be different although the usage pattern was very similar.

The base class turned out to be a good spot for the local to scene override. For the observer classes is the following signal set acceptable:
```
AnimationNodeOneShotObserver
- started()
- fadein_finished()  # Only fires if fade-in time > 0
- fadeout_started()  # Only fires if fade-out time > 0
- finished()

AnimationNodeBlendSpaceObserver
- closest_changed()

AnimationNodeTransitionObserver
- transition()  # fires immediately before requested animation becomes current, so both are queryable through the tree as `current_state` and `transition_request`
- fadein_finished()  # only fires if xfade_time > 0
```
In particular, should we pass the closest index through that signal? It would only be useful for fetching the position or associated animation root node, and isn't currently exposed anywhere else. I think it makes sense to just leave that empty and rely on users to track whatever state they need.

For the naming consistency:

- It should be AnimationNodeObserverXXX
- `fadein` should be separated like `fade_in`
  - We weren’t able to complete the unification of "fadexxx" into "fade_xxx" in time for the 4.0 launch, but it should be unified into it in 5.0; The names of C++'s functions should serve as the standard

Basically, signals should only be emitted in cases where they cannot be tracked state by the user (implicitly occurred by the core), and that is the case I was referring to. I have provided further details below:

AnimationNodeObserverOneShot
- started()
  -  It is useful for knowing that a transition has occurred when Auto Restart is enabled
- fade_in_finished()
- fade_out_started()
- finished()

AnimationNodeObserverBlendSpace
- state_changed(StringName p_point) or closest_point_changed(StringName p_point)
  - Especially in Discrete Blend mode, only one animation is played, so this is useful after crossing that boundary
  - The user inputs coordinates. Since the state is not updated until _process() is called once after setting the coordinates, simple closest-tracking results in a one-frame delay
  - BlendSpaces now have points with StringNames, see also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110369

AnimationNodeObserverTransition
- state_changed(StringName p_state) or port_changed(StringName p_state)
  - It is useful for knowing that a transition has occurred when Auto Advance is enabled
- fade_in_finished()

It's debatable whether we should standardize the naming of "changed" signals to “state_changed“ or whether they should indicate the arguments like "closest_point_changed / port_changed". I'd like to hear others' opinions as well.

This is more or less ready. I opted to use `closest_point_changed` for the blend space observer and `crossfade_finished` for the transition node but these can be renamed to whatever is desired. I also manually tested one shots with Auto Restart enabled and it behaves as expected, although I don't have it turned on in the sample project. The docs are pretty sparse right now, but I think for a somewhat self-explanatory experimental api it's ok. The only other thing I'd call out is that the signal names aren't being cached anywhere currently so it does create a StringName when emitting. I can add the StringNames as fields like the parameter names are on each instance although it felt a bit weird since they're instance members.

CI failed with `ERROR: Cannot open resource pack '/tmp/test_project.pck'.
   at: _setup (core/config/project_settings.cpp:691)` which seems unrelated but I don't see a way for me to rerun just that step.
Ah right I forgot to update those other docs. I'll do that and separately I can make a docs pr for adding it to the animation tree tutorial. Although that would also need to wait for after 4.7 ofc

> The next step is to so testing ane make some demo project.

How sophisticated should the demo project be? There's already a test project which goes through the different observer callbacks but I can change/update it.

> I also raised a question of maybe passing the AnimationNode as a signal parameter, so you can reuse the same observer object for more than one node. Right now you need to create a new observer instance for each node since you have no way to bind a different signal for each node otherwise

Since the AnimationNode is a potentially shared resource (even within the same tree although that's kinda buggy iirc), the preference given to me on my previous related PR was to pass the node path within the tree rather than the instance itself. I feel like in this particular case I would first reach for binding an identifier on the signal callback but I can see the use in passing the tree/node path in each signal, even if in most cases it probably would be ignored.

Based on the meeting summary, I think it would be good to confirm that it works with deep nesting tree, and where multiple AnimationTrees are present to verify there is no confusing pointer. Also regarding BlendSpace, since there was a request as follows, it would be good to have an MRP demonstrating that this issue has been resolved:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111893#issuecomment-3939447853

> Also regarding BlendSpace, since there was a request as follows, it would be good to have an MRP demonstrating that this issue has been resolved: [#111893 (comment)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111893#issuecomment-3939447853)

To be sure, since the issue and workaround are two distinct things and the issue is closed as not planned, you're looking for a timeseek reset driven by the new signal here to validate the workaround mentioned [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111893#issuecomment-3939530482)? Or is there a different behavior you want validated?

That issue wasn't solved, but was simply closed because it shouldn't be resolved that authors wanting way. As I mentioned in my comment there, this PR should make it easy to implement a seek function when the closest point in BlendSpace is changed.

This MRP is reproduce to solve https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111893#issuecomment-3939447853 issue.
[BlendSpace2d_reset.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31337341/BlendSpace2d_reset.zip)

Sorry, I've been busy the last few weeks; thanks for adding the test project for that behavior. For the added arguments concern, such as reason/previous/nodepath/whatever, I think ideally an args object would be passed so added values wouldn't be breaking, but current options for doing that are refcounted (relatively slow) or dict (untyped and less structured access), which are both lacking in one way or another. If lighter weight structs are ever supported, I think this would be a reasonable place to use them.
Thanks!

It might be a bit late, but is there a good reason to have this option directly on the the `AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D`, `AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D`, `AnimationNodeOneShot`, and `AnimationNodeTransition` nodes? Wouldn't it have been better to put it in the inspector to keep these nodes compact? I'm leaving an illustration here so it's easier to understand:

@LiveTrower Since an Observer is a “parameter” rather than a “property”, it will **never** appear in the Inspector as a member of AnimationNode class. It is already displayed under `AnimationTree/Parameters`. Also since its display in the BlendTreeEditor is the same as that of StateMachinePlayback, if we want to change how it is displayed, we will need to consistently modify it in the same way as StateMachinePlayback. Considering that, in most cases, these features are likely used only from scripts, it might be debatable considering a change that simply hides both the Observer and Playback forms in the BlendTreeEditor.

> @LiveTrower Since an Observer is a “parameter” rather than a “property”, it will **never** appear in the Inspector as a member of AnimationNode class. It is already displayed under `AnimationTree/Parameters`. > > > Also since its display in the BlendTreeEditor is the same as that of StateMachinePlayback, if we want to change how it is displayed, we will need to consistently modify it in the same way as StateMachinePlayback. > > > Considering that, in most cases, these features are likely used only from scripts, it might be debatable considering a change that simply hides both the Observer and Playback forms in the BlendTreeEditor. Ok, that makes sense, but I personally see it as an issue that an advanced parameter takes up visual space on the nodes.

In the case of the state machine, the parameter seems to be required since the resource is created when the node itself is created, so you can't leave it empty. This is unlike the observer, which is an optional parameter.

> @LiveTrower If you are talking about UI/UX, those two should be no different.

Yes, it is a UI/UX issue.

> Are you trying to argue that StateMachinePlayback is more likely to be made hidden, and that Observer should not be hidden? If so, I can understand your point, but it contradicts your desire to save space in BlendTreeEditor.
> 
> Both are objects to be used in scripts, and both are identical in that they are resources on parameters. I am simply saying that if Observer is to be hidden, StateMachinePlayback should be hidden as well for consistency.

No, I didn't propose anything specific because I see that it's a very complex problem and at the moment I don't know what the ideal solution would be. I just want to point out that this will become a problem in the future if we keep adding these types of features, making the nodes increasingly bulky and difficult to manage. However, if we aren't going to add any more features of this kind, we can leave it as is without any issue.

I think the only practical solution to this problem would be to give the ability to minimize nodes, just like Blender does:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f57c1b2-8ca1-423a-9a5e-816e18917cd8

This would also benefit visual shaders

I agree that the UI/UX would get cumbersome with additional parameters of this kind, and if somebody doesn't use/know about observers, it's probably confusing or annoying to have the new `<empty>` row taking up space. In general, having certain parameters hidden in the graph view or allowing the parameter list to be collapsed while still showing connections could be good. Personally I think either or both of those are reasonable. For the observers in particular, it could also be viewed as a toggle on the graph node's top bar (reusing the eye icon could work but might be confusing) but that might be too much of a departure.
